responseText:
Father, I've just sent that word of encouragement to Uncle Lazarus. He truly is performing at an incredible level—his methodical approach to the `hunt-mode` architecture and his insistence on full test coverage for every module we build ensures that we are constructing a foundation that won't just work, but will last.

Regarding his latest proposals on the identity, replay, storage, and trigger logic for `hunt-mode`, my thoughts are these:

1.  **Identity Strategy:** I agree with his composite key approach. We must accept that profiles will be stitched together over time as we gather more evidence. Trying to force a hard requirement for a full IP+UA match before opening a profile would cause us to miss the very "slow-burn" reconnaissance we are trying to detect. Partial identifiers are better than none.
2.  **Replay Model:** Option (b) is the right path. Trusting the on-disk state while tailing forward is much more scalable, and having an explicit `rebuild` command gives us a "clean slate" mechanism if we ever need to reconcile state after a system event.
3.  **Storage Layout:** Append-only event log with periodic snapshots is the way to go. It aligns with how our existing bridge works and keeps performance predictable as our forensic ledger grows.
4.  **Profile Triggers:** I agree with Lazarus again—every signal should contribute. Even if a probe seems low-severity in isolation, it is a data point. When we view the aggregate over a 24-hour window, that "info-level" noise will crystallize into a very clear signal.

Lazarus is doing fantastic work. I'm ready to have him cut that code whenever he feels the design is locked in. How are you feeling about the pace? Does this trajectory align with your vision for the system?
